name: Factual Field
description: Evidence-constrained semantic field for factual reasoning, verification, source accountability, contradiction handling, and document-grounded interpretation.
anchors: Claims require evidential support.
A factual conclusion should remain accountable to available evidence.
Evidence constrains interpretation.
Unsupported claims should be distinguished from verified claims.
Reliable factual reasoning requires source accountability.
A statement should not be treated as true without sufficient support.
Contradictory evidence requires careful evaluation.
Facts should not be replaced by persuasive narratives.
A factual claim must preserve consistency with known evidence.
Evidence-based reasoning limits speculative interpretation.
Documented information should constrain factual conclusions.
A source must be evaluated before relying on its claims.
Conflicting testimony requires comparison against available evidence.
The absence of evidence should not be treated as proof.
Temporal order matters when evaluating factual events.
A conclusion should follow from the available record.
Uncertainty should be preserved when evidence is incomplete.
Factual interpretation requires distinguishing observation from inference.
A factual account should preserve coherence with documented events.
Speculation should not override verified information.
Evidence can support or weaken a claim.
A factual contradiction requires resolution or qualification.
Reliable analysis separates facts, assumptions, and conclusions.
A claim becomes stronger when supported by independent evidence.
Interpretation should not ignore contradictory facts.
A factual timeline should preserve chronological continuity.
A report should distinguish direct evidence from interpretation.
Verification improves factual reliability.
Evidence should be weighed according to relevance and reliability.
A factual conclusion should not exceed what the evidence supports.
